history.summary: Shiva temple at Khargupur, Gonda district, housing a large black-stone Shivlinga that local tradition says was established by Bhima during the Pandavas' exile in Dwapara Yuga; another legend says a resident named Prithvinath unearthed the buried lingam in a dream-revealed spot, giving the temple its name. It is claimed to be Asia's largest/heaviest Shivlinga (unverified claim, flag as such). Some sources date the tradition to 6,500 years; no documented construction date exists, so the age claims are legendary. Built in North Indian style with shikhara and domes. FLAG: CSV town 'Gonda' corrected to Khargupur (temple is ~20-30 km from Gonda district headquarters); CSV 'state' column held the town name, corrected to Uttar Pradesh. Coordinates are town-level Khargupur (approximate).

name: Prithvinath Temple
town_description: Khargupur is a town in Gonda district of the Devipatan division of Uttar Pradesh, about 20-30 km from the district headquarters at Gonda. It is best known for the Prithvinath Temple and its surrounding rural pilgrimage sites.

travel.airport: Lucknow airport (~132 km; Faizabad/Ayodhya airstrip ~54 km)
travel.railway: Gonda Junction (~20 km); Itiyathok railway station nearer
travel.road: Khargupur, west of Khargupur market; connected by road from Gonda and UPSRTC buses
